confirmed_fact: Southampton City Council is a unitary authority responsible for all local services in the city, around 700 services in total.

topic: What can be reported as street cleaning
confirmed_fact: Fly-tipping, dog fouling, dead animals, spillages, broken glass and other dangerous items seen on a road, pavement or public space in Southampton can be reported as a street cleaning problem.
caveat: The page does not say whether private land is covered.

category_id: fly_tipping; dog_fouling; dead_animal; litter_street_cleaning; graffiti_flyposting; glass_spillage_hazard
confirmed_fact: The council aims to deal with at least 75% of urgent street cleaning requests within one working day of being reported.
caveat: This is an aim, not a guarantee.

confirmed_fact: Graffiti and fly-posting will also be investigated by the council.
The council takes reports of abandoned vehicles and of problems with a road or pavement such as a pothole.
caveat: The page does not give criteria for abandoned vehicles.

confirmed_fact: The council gives advice and may be able to help with problems from a neighbouring property such as noise, light, dust, smoke or odours.
caveat: The wording is may be able to help, not a promise of action.

confirmed_fact: Concerns about a property that has become very dirty, with possible rodent infestations, or where hoarded possessions make access difficult can be reported for investigation.

The council environment section also covers pest control, trees, grass, hedges and leaves, a Tree Preservation Order map, animal welfare, pollution, parks and open spaces, and emergencies and severe weather.
caveat: Only the section headings were read, not each page.

confirmed_fact: The council has local street cleansing teams and a separate commercial street cleansing service.
caveat: Only the section menu was read.

confirmed_fact: The fixed penalty for fly-tipping is 400 pounds, reduced to 250 pounds if paid within ten days of the notice being issued.
caveat: National limits can change. Re-check on the day.

confirmed_fact: The council defines fly-tipping as waste greater than one black sack left on land without the owner's permission.
caveat: The page does not mention private land specifically.

confirmed_fact: A fixed penalty can be issued to anyone who allows their waste to be fly-tipped. The page gives the example of using someone found online to dispose of waste without getting their full details and a receipt.
caveat: The page does not mention licensed waste carriers or transfer notes.

confirmed_fact: On public land the council's specialist reactive team removes graffiti and fly-posting. Street cleansing teams and Neighbourhood Wardens use graffiti wipes on small graffiti, and the council issues wipes to local individuals and groups.

The council does not fund or resource graffiti removal on private or commercial property as a core service. It can advise owners, and owners or businesses can request help from the specialist team through a form that leads to a request for a quote.
caveat: The cost of a quote is not stated.

confirmed_fact: The council aims to remove racist, obscene or hate crime graffiti within one working day of a report and other graffiti within two weeks.
caveat: The page states these under public land reporting.

confirmed_fact: Graffiti on BT or Openreach street cabinets should be reported to Openreach on 0800 023 2023 and on Virgin Media cabinets to Virgin Media on 0330 333 0444. Graffiti on bus shelters or railway bridges should be reported to the company responsible, not the council.
caveat: Confirmed for graffiti on this equipment only, not for general faults.

confirmed_fact: Roads: under 4cm is monitored and not automatically repaired, 4 to 7.5cm is repaired within 6 months, over 7.5cm within 24 hours. Pavements: under 2cm is monitored, 2 to 4cm within 6 months, over 4cm within 24 hours. Staff aim to assess a report within two weeks, emergencies get a temporary repair within 24 hours, and the council tries to repair non-urgent potholes within two months where possible.
caveat: The page does not mention private roads, motorways or trunk roads.

confirmed_fact: The council announced an 11.9 million pound highways and footways programme for 2023/24 and reported 5,204 potholes repaired in the previous 12 months and over 1.4 million pounds spent on dedicated pothole repair. It names Balfour Beatty Living Places as its highways partner carrying out much of the work. It also reports gritting winter routes, traffic signal improvements on Thomas Lewis Way and 20mph signage.
source_name: 11.9 million confirmed for highways and footways programme during 2023/2024
caveat: This is a 2023/24 news article, so figures are not current. It does not list street lighting or drainage.

confirmed_fact: Before reporting, residents should check the bin was out on the correct day, was clearly visible to the crew, is a council-supplied bin, and that the report is within two working days of the collection day. The council aims to return for a missed collection within two to five working days.

If the wrong bin was put out, or the bin contained contamination or items the council cannot collect such as rubble or clinical waste, the bin is not treated as missed. Contamination must be removed and the bin is collected on the next scheduled day.
The council Leader published a notice about disruption to household waste collections in patches of the city and urged residents to keep reporting missed collections online.
source_name: Important update on waste collections from Councillor Fielker
caveat: The page was undated when read. Check whether it is still current.

confirmed_fact: Homes with bin storage should have a green-top general waste bin, a blue-top recycling bin and a black or grey glass box. Homes without storage get rolls of sacks delivered twice a year. Before reporting a missing bin residents are asked to check whether it was moved, claimed by a neighbour or returned to the wrong property.

A lost or stolen general waste (green-lidded) bin costs 33 pounds for 140 litre, 43 pounds for 240 litre and 54 pounds for 360 litre. Charges are non-refundable. Glass and recycling bins can be replaced free.
source_name: My bin is lost or stolen
caveat: The page does not say whether damaged bins are free.

confirmed_fact: Tenants, not landlords, are responsible for making sure household waste is disposed of properly. Everyone in the house shares responsibility for the right waste in the bins, putting them out and bringing them back in. Bins repeatedly left on the street can lead to a 60 pound fine.
source_name: Information for students about household waste
caveat: Re-check the fine amount before the demo.

confirmed_fact: The council has an online form to report a repair for council tenants and leaseholders.
caveat: Only the form title was seen.

confirmed_fact: Call 023 8023 3344 for council housing emergency repairs outside office hours. The same line covers children's services, community alarm, community care, emergency planning, highways, homelessness caused by an emergency, the register office and trees. Textphone users dial 18001 first. Adult social care is 0300 555 1373.

The council prefers audio recordings uploaded through its Noise App. Paper log sheets are accepted only in exceptional cases. Evidence is due within 28 days. If it does not show a likely statutory nuisance, or none is provided, the council takes no further action and does not reinvestigate for three calendar months. Officers may also visit or install a recording device.

Excluded noise includes children playing or crying, neighbours talking, snoring, impact noise in shared buildings, daytime domestic appliances and DIY (roughly 0700 to 2200), garden equipment, one-off parties, traffic, aircraft, fireworks and wild animals such as seagulls. A service manager can allow an excluded complaint in exceptional circumstances.

Complaints from business representatives are investigated. For commercial or industrial noise officers first consider early engagement with the operator. The protocol treats licensed entertainment venues as commercial premises and may refer them to licensing services.
The protocol applies section 79 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and uses an average person test, weighing the type of noise, frequency, time of day and the character of the area.
The council names itself as Lead Local Flood Authority and has a report a flood section on its flood risk management page.
caveat: The page does not say what the role covers or how to report blocked drains or road flooding.

confirmed_fact: The gas emergency number is 0800 111 999. It is free and open 24 hours a day. National Gas lists the official safety steps on the same page.
caveat: Link to the page for safety advice. Do not rewrite the steps.

confirmed_fact: Call 105 to report a power cut or damage to electricity equipment. Lines are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
caveat: The page does not list the areas SSEN covers.

confirmed_fact: Southern Water gives 0800 820 999 for urgent leaks such as a burst pipe or water flowing quickly across the ground.
caveat: The page does not give opening hours or a number for sewer flooding.

confirmed_fact: Report one pothole per form. Staff assess within about two weeks. Emergency defects get a temporary repair within 24 hours; most are non-urgent, programmed within six months (aim two). White marking means already inspected. Form needs location, depth and ideally a photo.
Private land or property fly-tipping must be resolved by the owner or occupier; form is for public land or witnessed fly-tips with evidence of who did it.
Council disposes of dead animals on council-owned or managed land, including pets and wild animals. On a busy carriageway tell them it is a traffic hazard. Private land is the owner's responsibility.
Report to the retailer first; council removes only badly damaged untraceable trolleys, as fly-tipping.
Leaves cleared Oct to mid-Jan; reports actioned only for serious hazard or flood risk; photo helps.
Hate/obscene graffiti aimed within 1 working day, other graffiti within 2 weeks. Private/commercial graffiti not in core service.

Vehicle must not be in use; inspected usually within a week (burnt out within 24 hours); untaxed investigations take 4-8 weeks; no guarantee of removal; reporter needs contact details and registration number.
caveat: Council cannot tell the reporter the outcome.

confirmed_fact: Form covers blocked driveway/dropped kerb, zig-zags, yellow lines, no permit in controlled zone, double parking, disabled bay without badge, bus stop/taxi rank, loading/EV/suspended bays. Needs registration, colour, make, photos. Dropped kerb PCN £70.
